subject: Discovery recap & bake-off next steps (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-20T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap & bake-off next steps

Hi John (and Sally),

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the candid discussion about the inference issues you're seeing in production. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps for the bake-off. Let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you called out:
- Unpredictable p95 latency under realistic traffic (spiky qps) when using vLLM on self-hosted instances.
- Higher token/unit cost than expected for peak workloads (esp. long-context prompts).
- Occasional memory/KV cache pressure causing request failures during sustained traffic.
- Need for deterministic fallbacks and smoother degradation across model variants.

Current stack + constraints:
- Customer-managed vLLM deployments (self-hosted on EC2) and occasional runs on TGI endpoints for batch jobs.
- Strict regulatory requirement to keep PII out of external logs; any hosted test must respect this.
- Targeted production throughput: ~500 concurrent requests, typical batch of 1–8 tokens per request but many long-context sessions (avg 1k tokens/session).

Success criteria you asked for (qualitative and quantitative):
- p95 latency <= 200 ms for conversational requests at target throughput (500 concurrent).
- No request error rate above 0.5% under steady-state for the benchmark runs.
- Cost per 1M generated tokens comparable or lower than your current vLLM + infra baseline.
- Quality parity: <5% regression on your acceptance prompt set (we'll use your sample prompts for evaluation).

Bake-off ask / proposed scope:
- Redwood will run a 10-business-day bake-off comparing: (A) Redwood Dedicated/Hosted inference (Redwood-managed variant) vs (B) your current vLLM self-hosted baseline vs (C) TGI cloud endpoints (if you want included).
- We'll use the sample prompt set you provide and a synthetic traffic pattern that matches your qps spikes.
- Deliverables: raw benchmark CSVs (latency percentiles, throughput, error rates), cost estimates (in USD) normalized to 1M tokens, quality evaluation results on acceptance prompts, and a short runbook with recommended config (batching, quantization profile).

What we need from you to start:
1) Sample prompt set + <= 1000 representative sessions (s3 link or Drive).
2) Baseline vLLM/TGI run config (instance types, concurrency config) or permission to reproduce the configuration.
3) Confirmation that A/B tests may use anonymized samples and that Redwood can run the hosted tests under a shared but PII-scrubbed dataset.

Timeline propose: once we have the dataset and baselines, Redwood will kick off the bake-off within 3 business days and deliver first results within 7 business days of start.

Attachments: acme_sample_requests.xlsx (request checklist), 20250620-acme-call-notes.pdf (internal call notes).

Next steps / owners:
- John / Sally: share sample prompts + baseline configs (S3 or Drive link).
- Marissa (me): coordinate kickoff and keep weekly status.
- Dev: build benchmark scripts and propose exact invocation parameters.

Would love confirmation of the above and timeline preferences.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

---
From: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sally Chen <sally.chen@acme.com>
Date: 2025-06-21T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & bake-off next steps

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. This matches our notes and priorities. A few clarifications: 

- The p95 <= 200 ms target is for our 1k token average session size, correct? We do see slightly better numbers for short exchanges but the long-context sessions are where vLLM spikes. 
- For cost comparison, please include equivalent cost modeling for reserved EC2 vs on-demand vs Redwood Dedicated as separate rows — we care about monthly run-rate not just per-batch.
- We are happy to include TGI cloud endpoints in the bake-off; please make the comparison explicit in the deliverables.

I'll share the sample prompt set (S3 link) and our vLLM run config by end of day tomorrow. One ask: can you include a quality check focusing on hallucination rate on our 50 acceptance prompts? We can provide the ground-truth answers for scoring.

Sally will own the dataset handoff.

Thanks,
John
VP, AI Platforms | Acme Corp
john.smith@acme.com

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap & bake-off next steps (internal)

Quick internal — forwarding the customer confirmation. Goal: design a bake-off that gives deterministic comparisons vs vLLM and TGI. Dev, can you draft the benchmark harness and config matrix? Items I want covered:

- Workloads: 3 traffic profiles (spiky conversational, steady long-context, batch generation).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), error rate, memory pressure events, cost (USD per 1M tokens) normalized to reserved vs on-demand.
- Quality: hallucination rate on the 50 acceptance prompts + ROUGE/BLEU where applicable.
- Comparison targets: vLLM (self-hosted, exact instance types Sally will send), TGI endpoints (cloud), Redwood hosted/dedicated variants.

Dev — please include exact Docker/command-line reproducible steps and a script to ingest Acme's prompts (PII-scrubbed). Let's aim to have a draft plan by EOD Friday (2025-06-27).

Thanks — Marissa

---
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-23T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed bake-off plan & benchmarks (Acme)

John / Marissa — attaching the proposed bake-off plan and the benchmark harness overview. High level plan below and link to shared doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEXAMPLE

Planned benchmark matrix:
- Profiles: spiky_conv (peaks to 800 qps), steady_long (500 concurrent sessions, avg 1k tokens/session), batch_gen (large batched jobs, throughput focused).
- Systems compared: 1) Acme vLLM self-hosted baseline (as-configured), 2) TGI cloud endpoints (standard config), 3) Redwood Dedicated (optimized batching + KV caching), 4) Redwood Private (optional if you want us to mirror your infra).

Metrics collected:
- p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) per workload
- tokens/sec and CPU/GPU utilization
- error rate (%) and memory/KV cache eviction events
- quality: hallucination rate on the 50 acceptance prompts, plus summary metrics (precision recall / token-level differences)
- cost: normalized USD per 1M tokens using on-demand pricing + reserved scenarios

Execution & timeline:
- Start: target Monday 2025-06-30 (once we receive the S3 dataset + your vLLM instance types).
- Run length: 10 business days for repeated runs and edge-case tests.
- Deliverables: benchmark CSVs, a short slide summary, cost model, and a runbook.
- Review meeting: propose Wed 2025-07-16 to walk results and next steps.

Attachments: redwood_bakeoff_plan.md (detailed scripts + invocation examples).

Notes on comparison to vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints:
- We'll reproduce vLLM locally with the same quantization/instance types you provide; where exact reproduction isn't possible we'll note assumptions.
- For TGI endpoints, we will run against public endpoints (or customer-provided endpoint keys) and normalize for instance class differences.

Action items:
- John/Sally: send S3 link and vLLM config by EOD 2025-06-24.
- Marissa: confirm the kickoff date and whether Redwood can run hosted comparisons on scrubbed dataset.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you'd like to walk the plan.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
